title: Unique formal kernel product section for fixed inputs
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and $F=(\mathcal F_r)_{r\geq 1}$ a coherent formal module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Write $B_m=\mathcal I^m/\mathcal I^{m+1}$, $K_0=\mathcal F_1$, $K_n=\ker(\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n)$ for $n>0$, with projections $\pi_m$ and inclusions $\iota_n$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-kernel-graded-pieces], in sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Fix $m,n\geq0$, an open $U$, $a\in B_m(U)$, and $x\in K_n(U)$. There is a unique $y\in K_{m+n}(U)$ such that for every $V\subseteq U$, every $a^{\prime}\in\mathcal I^m(V)$ with $\pi_m(a^{\prime})=a|_V$, and every $t\in\mathcal F_{m+n+1}(V)$ whose reduction to $\mathcal F_{n+1}(V)$ equals $\iota_n(x|_V)$, one has $\iota_{m+n}(y|_V)=a^{\prime}t$. This asserts a product for two fixed sections, without any linearity or compatibility between different input pairs.

source.place: Lemma 087Z (lemma-finite-over-rees-algebra), its associated graded construction, and Section 0EHN; expanded local-lift argument. Source read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087Z and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EHN.

proof.text: Prove restriction stability of the universal equation using PresheafOfModules.map_comp_apply. Obtain local simultaneous coefficient and transition lifts using the proved private formal_transition_epi and local_lifts_three helpers from FormalKernelBilinearActionAssociative (import all). Coefficient projections are cokernel projections and hence epi. The transition epimorphism proof uses only the defining adjacent quotient isomorphisms, not any stalk quotient identification.

For actual coefficient and transition representatives apply the representative-product lemma to obtain a kernel section. On every smaller open restrict both representatives. Naturality of the projection and transition identifies the restricted classes. Apply the independence clause there; naturality of the kernel inclusion and semilinearity of restriction give the universal equation.

Prove uniqueness independently of existence: near each point simultaneously lift the coefficient section and the kernel inclusion through the transition. Any two outputs satisfying the universal equation have the same inclusion on this neighbourhood. Cancel the sectionwise injective kernel inclusion and use TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq' to conclude equality. Restrict local products to pairwise intersections and apply this uniqueness result to establish compatibility. TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing' produces their global gluing.

For arbitrary smaller W and arbitrary representatives on W, compare the desired formula on W intersected with each member of the gluing cover. Naturality moves the kernel inclusion through restriction, and the gluing equations identify the restricted global output with the local product. Restrict the specified representatives and apply the local universal equation. The intersections cover W, so sheaf separation gives the formula on W. The preceding uniqueness proof finishes ExistsUnique. Subtype indexing and empty covers handle empty opens without an extra assumption.

theorem formalKernel_product_section_existsUnique {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : CoherentFormalModule X I) (m n : ℕ) (U : X.Opens)
    (a : (formalAssociatedGradedPiece I m).val.obj (op U))
    (x : (formalKernelPiece F n).val.obj (op U)) :
    ∃! y : (formalKernelPiece F (m + n)).val.obj (op U),
      ∀ (V : X.Opens) (h : V ≤ U)
        (a' : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).1.val.obj (op V))
        (t : (F.obj.obj (op (m + n))).val.obj (op V)),
        (formalAssociatedGradedπ I m).val.app (op V) a' =
          (formalAssociatedGradedPiece I m).val.map (homOfLE h).op a →
        (F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_left n m)).op).val.app (op V) t =
          (formalKernelι F n).val.app (op V)
            ((formalKernelPiece F n).val.map (homOfLE h).op x) →
        (formalKernelι F (m + n)).val.app (op V)
          ((formalKernelPiece F (m + n)).val.map (homOfLE h).op y) =
            (@id Γ(X, V)
              ((Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2.val.app (op V) a')) • t
